title: Mata Sulakhni and the sons
hookLine: Nanak's wife raised their sons, Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das, while he traveled

cards: A journey story often has someone just outside the frame. The one who packed the food. The one who watched the road.
The one who answered the door when the neighbors came asking where he'd gone. The janamsakhis follow Guru Nanak and Mardana down long roads.
Today we turn around and look back at the house he left, and at the woman who kept it. Today: Mata Sulakhni.

teach.b: Her name was Sulakhni. Sikhs call her Mata Sulakhni, Mata meaning mother, the honor given to the women of the Gurus' households. She and Nanak had two sons, Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das.

teach.h: SHE STAYED AND KEPT THE HOUSE.
teach.b: When Nanak set out on his long journeys, she stayed. She raised the boys and kept the household going while Nanak, who had left his post at the storehouse, was on the road. The janamsakhis don't give her many lines.
Where she does appear, she's honest. Some tellings show her worry: a husband gone a long time on the road, children growing up with an empty place at the table.
Some have her asking him plainly what will become of her and the boys.

teach.h: HER QUESTION STAYS IN THE STORY.
teach.b: The stories keep that question in. They didn't polish it out. Now ask what the story knows.
Guru Nanak's own hymns praise the life of the householder, the one who earns honestly, shares, and remembers God in the middle of family life, rather than leaving the world behind.
And in Bhai Gurdas's telling, Nanak ends his travels at Kartarpur, back in ordinary clothes, working the fields with his family. So the road came home.
And while it was out there, someone at home was living the householder's life that the hymns describe, without a crowd and without a sakhi of her own. Sikhs remember her and honor her name.
She is the one who stayed. A long road often has one, and the story goes quiet where they stand.

how: Sikhs honor Mata Sulakhni as Guru Nanak's wife and the mother of Baba Sri Chand and Baba Lakhmi Das, and remember her in the stories of the Guru's household.

games.q: you're Mata Sulakhni. your husband has been on the road for a long time, and the boys are growing. what do you do?
o: leave the house to follow him.
stay, raise the boys and keep the house going.
return to your parents and wait.
games.why: the tradition remembers her staying and raising Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das, and some tellings keep her worried question to Nanak in the story.

practice: Let one face come to you: a parent who worked the night shift, a grandmother who cooked for everyone, a partner who held things together while you were away, a sibling who stayed close to the family.
See them for a moment doing the ordinary thing they did, and silently name one thing they did that nobody wrote down. If you pray, you can say Waheguru with them in mind.

wordCard.voice: Mata Sulakhni, Guru Nanak's wife, who stayed and raised Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das while he traveled.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi: mother. Sikhs use it as a title of honor for the women of the Gurus' households.

carryVoice: Your line: the one who stayed. The householder's life, lived without a crowd. See you tomorrow.
